chapter.title: The Borrowed Hour
chapter.subtitle: Alice enters a tea party that keeps borrowing tomorrow to avoid ending today.
chapter.description: Alice enters a tea party that keeps borrowing tomorrow to avoid ending today.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: My receipt says I arrived twelve minutes from now. They’ve already charged a late fee.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: Service is terrible. You haven’t complained yet and they’ve blocked you.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: Who owns this café?

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: Follow the invoice. That’s how everyone gets to the Queen.

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: The cake makes me tall. One whole bottle makes me tiny, no matter how tall I started. The key’s on a high shelf.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: The door says PLEASE STOP KICKING ME.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: The door knows what it did.

puzzle.title: Do not shrink without the key
puzzle.instruction: Start ordinary-sized. Use every action once. Cake makes Alice tall; drinking the WHOLE bottle makes her tiny from any starting size. Only tall Alice reaches the key; only tiny Alice reaches the lock and fits the doorway.

pieces.label: Pocket the key
pieces.detail: Requires tall size. Once pocketed, it changes size with Alice.

pieces.label: Eat the cake
pieces.detail: Changes size to tall. The bottle and key can be carried afterward.

pieces.label: Cross the doorway
pieces.detail: Requires tiny size and an unlocked door.

pieces.label: Drink the whole bottle
pieces.detail: Changes size to tiny. The bottle is used up.

pieces.label: Turn the key
pieces.detail: Requires tiny size AND the pocketed key. Unlocks the door.

hints: Shrinking is irreversible here, so check what must be collected first.
Cake → key → bottle leaves Alice tiny with the key.
puzzle.solvedText: Alice exits with the key in her pocket. The door requests that future complaints be made in writing, away from its hinges.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: The Queen lends each guest an hour. Then she charges another hour for staying to pay. I have been at brunch since Thursday.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: It’s Tuesday.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: I know. My eggs have a pension.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: Where is the clock spring?

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

preDialogue.speaker: Cheshire
preDialogue.text: Host keeps the clock key in the table’s prize box. Win the service game, box opens. Round three takes one Motion: the Queen calls it gratuity.

preDialogue.speaker: Alice
preDialogue.text: A mandatory tip to leave. She got bottle-service morals.

postDialogue.speaker: Cheshire
postDialogue.text: Clock key, three spoons, invoice for the silence after your joke.

postDialogue.speaker: Alice
postDialogue.text: Keep the invoice. We’re going to need proof of how stupid this gets.

passive.name: The Tea Service Trial
passive.description: Both sides receive 1 less Motion in round three.

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: Someone hid the clock spring in a cup. The table photo has the seats; the receipts have the drinks. Match them without swallowing the evidence.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: That feels directed at me.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: You ate a saucer.

puzzle.title: Four cups, one stolen spring
puzzle.instruction: Assign cups to Alice, Cheshire, Clockkeeper, Queen in that order. Alice refuses hot drinks. Clockkeeper needs a spoon to time his shift. Cheshire’s cup weighs nothing. Nobody shares.

pieces.label: Rose tea
pieces.detail: Hot. Liquid. No spoon. A metal glint under the crown-shaped sugar.

pieces.label: Empty cup
pieces.detail: No liquid, no spoon, no weight. Somehow still on the bill.

pieces.label: Black tea
pieces.detail: Hot. Liquid. Contains the table’s only spoon.

hints: Start with weight and temperature; two cups are forced.
Only black tea has the Clockkeeper’s spoon. Rose tea is left for the Queen.
puzzle.solvedText: The spring is in the Queen’s rose tea. Her own cup stopped the clock while she billed everyone for staying.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: I could leave through the wall. Been able to all day.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: Then why are you here?

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: Last time I left early, she posted “some people show you who they are” with my silhouette.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: You’re a floating grin. That could be any dental practice. Get your coat.

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: Spring recovered. Her clock stores borrowed hours in six numbered drawers. We reset them in order, everybody gets their afternoon back.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: Please find Thursday. My parking meter is raising my children.

puzzle.title: Give the hours back
puzzle.instruction: Arrange six hour-drawers from smallest debt to largest. Every drawer has a different whole-hour debt, 1 through 6. Read the relationships; the labels are amounts, not assembly directions.

pieces.label: Alice
pieces.detail: Owes twice the Clockkeeper’s debt, plus one.

pieces.label: Queen
pieces.detail: Owes six hours. She quietly borrowed from her own clock.

pieces.label: Door
pieces.detail: Owes one more hour than Clockkeeper. It stayed late for repairs.

pieces.label: Kitchen
pieces.detail: Owes one less than the Queen.

hints: Turn each relationship into a number before ordering.
Alice owes 3; Cheshire owes 4. Kitchen falls between Cheshire and Queen.
puzzle.solvedText: The drawers release 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 hours. The Queen owed the most. Her late-fee speech ages badly in real time.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

preDialogue.speaker: Alice
preDialogue.text: You printed that on a napkin. Fine. Goodbye game. Center closes in round three; we take the other exits.

preDialogue.speaker: Cheshire
preDialogue.text: Put my debt on her room. She owns the building.

postDialogue.speaker: Alice
postDialogue.text: Clock’s running. Doors open. Everybody take your leftovers.

postDialogue.speaker: Queen of Hearts
postDialogue.text: YOU WILL HEAR FROM MY COURT.

postDialogue.speaker: Cheshire
postDialogue.text: Can it email? I’m not coming back for tea.

passive.name: Permission to Leave
passive.description: The center district closes to new plays in round three.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: The summons says “You are hereby guilty of.” That’s it.

scenes.speaker: Cheshire
scenes.text: Leave the blank empty. She charges by the confession.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: I’m bringing the napkin, the receipts, and this cold biscuit. One of them is a weapon.
